description: Transactional job queue engine for Go with 10 storage backends, typed futures (await a job's result), composable local/global execution rate limits, crash recovery, pipelines, leader-safe scheduling, an admin dashboard, OpenTelemetry, and injected deterministic clocks.
rules: Import v2 paths: github.com/kirimatt/goncordia/v2 for the root and github.com/kirimatt/goncordia/driver/<name>/v2 for drivers
Use EnqueueTx (not Enqueue) when inside a database transaction — this is the transactional outbox pattern and guarantees the job appears only if the transaction commits
Use the in-memory driver (driver/memory) and gontest package for tests — no Docker or real database needed
To get a job's return value, register it with future.RegisterWorker, enqueue with future.Enqueue, and pass the future.Manager as WorkerConfig.Observer for instant local wake-up
Inject clock.Manual into the client, worker or scheduler, and driver in tests; Advance fires timers and tickers without sleeping
Redis, Cassandra, ClickHouse, and DynamoDB do not support transactional rollback; use Enqueue after commit for these backends
Mount admin.New(driver) behind application authentication; it exposes mutating job and queue actions
MongoDB requires a replica set — standalone MongoDB will fail at New()
SQLite requires db.SetMaxOpenConns(1) — only one writer allowed
Firestore requires a composite index created manually: collection goncordia_jobs, fields queue ASC + state ASC + run_at ASC
